title: "SHIELD Calibration and Container Pilot"
date: 2026-09-22
date-modified: 2026-10-05

**Status (2026-10-05):** Opt-in pilot on both owning default branches and
installed on one team server. It runs single-chain stages for one location at a
time from the team's committed analysis source, with frozen inputs and run
records. It does not yet run multi-chain stage 3, follow the team's
source-loaded engine, or launch a whole city list, so it is not yet usable for a
full calibration. A container usable for the team's real calibration workflows
is now the requested deliverable ([D-026](../decisions.qmd#d-026)). No
team member has run it yet.

This page keeps the current state and the evidence still in force. The full
dated record from 2026-09-17 to 2026-10-04 is preserved at
[wiki commit `bbe401b`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem-wiki/blob/bbe401bfaf1b3f3be6648abb5f9367e7ba1c17c4/investigations/shield-container-pilot.qmd).
The cross-repository [reproducibility contract](reproducibility.qmd) and
[manager selection](manager-compatibility.qmd) pages cover the wider design.
Implementation, tests, and runbooks live in `jheem_analyses` and
`jheem-containers`.

## Current state {#current-state}

| Capability | State (2026-10-05) |
|---|---|
| Recorded runs | Opt-in `SHIELD_RECORDED_RUN=true` path in `jheem_analyses`: declared source and package revisions, immutable manager releases verified by SHA-256, explicit seed, non-destructive `fresh`/`resume`. The ordinary launcher is unchanged when the flag is unset. |
| Run records | Per calibration: `inputs.json`, `outputs.json` (sizes and digests of the summary and simulation set), one record per attempt, and preceding-stage lineage. Completed stages are reused only after their files are re-verified. |
| Analysis source | A clean committed checkout is captured per pipeline and mounted read-only; continuations reuse it ([D-023](../decisions.qmd#d-023)). |
| Engine (`jheem2`) | Installed in the image at `9578726b`. The team loads jheem2 from source; snapshotting it like analysis source is next ([D-026](../decisions.qmd#d-026)). |
| Stages | Single-chain stages, alone or as an ordered pipeline that continues on rerun. Recorded mode refuses multi-chain calibrations (stage 3). |
| Installation | Two dated installations on shield2 (2026-10-01 and 2026-10-04), each verified, with both intended operator accounts checked and an administrator smoke run. No operator runs yet. |
| Hosted checks | Build, offline preflight, kill-and-resume, summary and assembly, two-stage lineage, numerical output inspection, missing/modified-output and changed-seed rejection, and a real stage-0 → stage-1 predecessor handoff. |

## Toward real calibrations {#operational-delivery}

The pilot's checks concentrate on single-chain stages that already run
natively. The remaining gaps are those between the pilot and the team's actual
workflow, in order:

1. **Engine from a source snapshot.** Capture the team's committed jheem2 checkout
   per pipeline, build it once per commit into a cached library without kept
   source references, record it, and reuse it on resume. Installed and
   hand-sourced engines agreed exactly at fixed parameters
   ([below](#engine-loading-comparison)).
2. **Multi-chain stage 3.** Set up once, run each chain as its own resumable
   process, and assemble only after every chain completes, with per-chain records
   and exclusive setup and assembly.
3. **Whole city list.** Launch a pipeline per location with a concurrency cap
   matching the team's launcher.
4. **Outputs in the team's analysis path.** Write where the team's analysis
   scripts read, or document how to point them at container outputs.
5. **Durable retention.** Source snapshots and records currently sit with the
   outputs on the NAS under a temporary directory. Later derived runs depend on
   them ([derived lineage](reproducibility.qmd#derived-lineage)).

The same-seed demonstration on real stages follows (see the
[validation plan](#repeatability-plan)). Shared writers across accounts still
need coordination beyond the wrapper's same-account check.

## Source selection {#separate-source}

Routine analysis edits don't need an image rebuild ([D-023](../decisions.qmd#d-023)).
First use of a calibration code captures a clean committed checkout; all its
locations in that output root share it, and a pipeline selects its stages
together. The archive and per-file hashes are kept under `run_sources/` beside the
records, verified before reuse, and mounted read-only. Dirty source, missing or
altered snapshots, incompatible selections, and changed saved inputs are refused.
A whole-repository snapshot takes about 580 MiB. On shield2, two calibration
definitions absent from the image completed with NAS state while the original
checkout was changed mid-run; both stages kept their captured source
([hosted check](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/actions/runs/36921240029),
[technical reference](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/blob/main/workloads/shield/SOURCE-SNAPSHOTS.md)).

Natively, each stage re-reads the live checkouts, so a multi-day pipeline can
mix code or data that changed between stages. A container pipeline uses one
captured selection for every stage and location.

## Reproducibility evidence {#repeatability-plan}

Same-seed claims depend on the comparison ([D-024](../decisions.qmd#d-024),
[D-025](../decisions.qmd#d-025)):

| Comparison | Measured | Next |
|---|---|---|
| Two fresh runs, same runtime and seed | Identical: initial values, chunk seeds, samples, likelihoods, adaptive state (eight-iteration fixture) | Repeat on a real stage |
| Uninterrupted vs interrupted and resumed | Diverged at iteration 4 ([below](#seed-replay-result)) | Owner-reviewed checkpoint/RNG proposal |
| Fixed parameters: installed vs hand-sourced engine | Identical within macOS and within Linux | — |
| Fixed parameters: Mac vs Linux | Up to about 1e-12 relative ([below](#engine-loading-comparison)) | — |
| Container vs native calibration | Not yet run | Compare stored chunk seeds first; agree statistical acceptance in advance |

The sampler's explicit seed argument is still ignored (chunk seeds come from the
ambient R state), but SHIELD calls `set.seed()` before setup, so a fixed workflow
can still repeat. The native launcher seeds at a different point than the recorded
one, so chunk seeds may differ even with the same seed value. In that case a
container-vs-native comparison can only be statistical. Across runtimes, tiny
numerical differences can flip an accept/reject decision, after which traces
separate. Native comparison targets must be runs that didn't resume mid-stage.

### Engine-loading comparison (2026-10-03) {#engine-loading-comparison}

The real Baltimore stage-1 likelihood was evaluated at three fixed parameter
vectors with identical manager bytes, recording 24,948 stratified outcome values
(four outcomes, 2010–2030, age × race × sex), 36 likelihood components, and three
totals. Installed-package and hand-sourced jheem2 `9578726b` agreed exactly
within macOS and within a Linux image
([run 37153878619](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/actions/runs/37153878619)).
Across platforms they differed slightly:

| Quantity | Largest absolute difference | Largest relative difference |
|---|---:|---:|
| Population cell | $1.89\times10^{-8}$ | $1.57\times10^{-13}$ |
| Incidence cell | $1.88\times10^{-10}$ | $6.57\times10^{-13}$ |
| Total-diagnosis cell | $2.03\times10^{-10}$ | $1.28\times10^{-12}$ |
| Primary/secondary-diagnosis cell | $1.33\times10^{-10}$ | $2.31\times10^{-12}$ |
| Likelihood component | $4.34\times10^{-10}$ | $1.34\times10^{-13}$ |
| Total log likelihood | $1.64\times10^{-9}$ | $4.65\times10^{-14}$ |

The environments differ in BLAS and compiler/platform details; individual causes
were not isolated. These are measurements, not an adopted tolerance.

### Seed and checkpoint replay result (2026-10-03) {#seed-replay-result}

Four isolated runs of the real Baltimore stage-0 model sampled two transmission
rates for eight iterations with four two-iteration checkpoints, in one image with
the same source and inputs
([run 37161484559](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/actions/runs/37161484559)).
Two fresh seed-0 runs matched exactly; seed 1 changed chunk seeds and samples.
An uninterrupted run and a twice-resumed run matched through the first
checkpoint, then accepted different proposals at iteration 4 (log likelihoods
−16484.35 vs −16475.78). Earlier checkpoints were unchanged and both runs completed.

**Mechanism:** a resumed process rebuilds its starting simulation after setting
the chunk seed and before drawing proposals; an uninterrupted process keeps it in
memory. In jheem2 `9578726b`, simulation metadata reads `calibrated.parameters`
while the kernel exposes `calibrated.parameter.names`
([`JHEEM_simulation.R`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/9578726b012a2ee380b380ef0203733d1bd81163/R/JHEEM_simulation.R#L1620-L1624),
[`JHEEM_kernel.R`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/9578726b012a2ee380b380ef0203733d1bd81163/R/JHEEM_kernel.R#L567-L573)),
so the rebuild draws a random metadata seed and shifts the proposal stream. A
sampler-only reproducer and short report are in
[`REPLAY-COMPARISON.md`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/bb93142ecc069e4094e3b130c23109babfb98730/applications/SHIELD/tests/REPLAY-COMPARISON.md).
Neither package was changed; a correction needs owner review. Resumed runs remain
operationally valid but are not trace-identical to uninterrupted ones.

## Earlier findings still in force

- **Install packages without kept source references.** With kept references, each
  stored simulation serialized about 5.6 GB of package state (about 20 MB
  natively), inflating checkpoints from about 5 MB to 266 MB and canary peak
  memory from 11 to 28.5 GB. The image build now fails if any team package keeps
  them, and the canary fails on oversized checkpoints.
- **Runtime parity.** A full 15,000-iteration stage-0 run on shield2 (before that
  fix) took a median 27.6 min per 500-iteration checkpoint against 29.9 min
  natively on shield1 (2026-09-30).
- **Server prerequisites** (RHEL 9, rootless Podman, SELinux enforcing): lingering
  per user, or rootless containers stop about 10 seconds after logout;
  `virt_use_samba` to reach the CIFS NAS; and keeping the user's `jheem` group in
  the container to write there.
- **The ordinary SHIELD test workflow** is not a gate. It fails at its static tier
  in every run (56 failures and 3 cancellations in the last 59 runs as of
  2026-10-05), mixing open review findings with checks, and skips later tiers.
- **Growth-penalty denominator.** The `start + 1` change is a scientific choice
  for zero and small baselines, for the model owners rather than infrastructure work.

## Open questions

- What statistical criteria define acceptable agreement between container and
  native calibrations?
- Where should source snapshots and run records be retained durably?
- Which current SHIELD checks can become a reliable must-pass subset, and which
  need scientific review?
- What behavior is intended for the growth penalty at a zero or near-zero baseline?
